claims.title: Engineer sign-in credentials may be intercepted if console access lacks transport encryption
claims.description: `flow:entity:duty-engineer>process:dispatch-console>open-console` carries the engineer's sign-in and is tagged with credentials, but its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. If this flow is not protected in transit, an attacker able to observe traffic on `boundary:corporate-network` can intercept the sign-in material between `entity:duty-engineer` and `process:dispatch-console`. The disclosed credentials could then enable access to the dispatch console and its subsequent calls to `process:dispatch-api`; this draft is conditional on resolving the unverified transport control.

quotes.text: Nobody wrote down how an engineer signs in to it.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `encryption_in_transit` is unknown on `flow:entity:duty-engineer>process:dispatch-console>open-console`, while an attacker still needs an on-path position on the corporate network. Impact is high because the flow carries credentials, which can provide access to the console and its dispatch capability.

mitigations.summary: Verify and require encrypted console sign-in transport
mitigations.detail: Establish the protocol and set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:entity:duty-engineer>process:dispatch-console>open-console` to TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation.
Use short-lived authenticated sessions, secure cookie flags where cookies are used, and MFA so intercepted sign-in material has limited value.

claims.title: Dispatch actions may be readable across the corporate-to-control-plane boundary
claims.description: `flow:process:dispatch-console>process:dispatch-api>dispatch-requests` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` to `boundary:production-control-plane` and carries dispatch actions, but its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. If the cross-origin console-to-API channel is not encrypted, an attacker positioned on that crossing can intercept requests that move crews or change a depot's work. The observed operational data can be used to map live dispatch activity and target subsequent attacks against `process:dispatch-api`; this draft is conditional on the transport-control gap.

quotes.text: The console calls the dispatch API.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses a trust boundary and has unknown transport encryption, though interception requires access to that path. Impact is medium because the intercepted requests expose business-critical dispatch actions affecting crew movements and depot work.

mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:dispatch-console>process:dispatch-api>dispatch-requests` to verified TLS 1.2+; use mTLS if the browser architecture is replaced by a service-to-service client.
Use opaque job and action references where possible, so captured request payloads reveal less about live operations.

claims.title: Live job status may be exposed on an unverified WebSocket crossing
claims.description: `flow:process:dispatch-console>process:dispatch-api>live-job-status` crosses from the corporate network to the production control plane and carries live job status, while its `encryption_in_transit` attribute is unknown. If the WebSocket is not upgraded over TLS, an on-path attacker can intercept the crews' live status sent to `process:dispatch-console`. That disclosure reveals current operational activity and can guide later targeting of crews, job orders, or the dispatch API; it is conditional on whether the socket is actually protected by TLS.

quotes.text: Nobody wrote down whether that socket runs over TLS

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the WebSocket crosses into the production control plane and its TLS status is unknown, but the attacker must obtain an on-path position. Impact is medium because the flow discloses business-critical live job status for crews on screen.

mitigations.detail: Use `wss://` with TLS 1.2+ and certificate validation for `flow:process:dispatch-console>process:dispatch-api>live-job-status`.

mitigations.summary: Revalidate session authorization for the socket
mitigations.detail: Authenticate the WebSocket handshake and revalidate the engineer session and authorization during the connection, limiting both exposure and stale-session access.

claims.title: Downloaded partner schedules may be intercepted before archive storage
claims.description: `flow:process:schedule-importer>store:schedule-archive>store-schedule-documents` writes the scheduling partner's XML work documents to `store:schedule-archive`, but its protocol and `encryption_in_transit` are unknown. If this internal write path lacks encryption, an attacker able to observe the corporate-network path can intercept the full schedule documents as they are archived. The schedules reveal planned work and can be correlated with the importer and dispatch API activity; this draft is conditional on the unverified transport protection.

quotes.text: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because both the internal protocol and transport encryption are unknown and the attacker must first gain an on-path position on the corporate network. Impact is medium because every intercepted document contains tomorrow's planned work, tagged as business-critical data.

mitigations.detail: Use an authenticated encrypted file or storage protocol for `flow:process:schedule-importer>store:schedule-archive>store-schedule-documents` and record the selected protocol and TLS posture.
Store only the document fields needed for operational retention and restrict network access to the archive path to the importer and authorized archive readers.

claims.title: A static importer API token may be exposed on the unverified control-plane crossing
claims.description: `flow:process:schedule-importer>process:dispatch-api>post-work-orders` crosses from `boundary:corporate-network` into `boundary:production-control-plane`, presents an API token, and has unknown `encryption_in_transit`. If transport protection is absent, an on-path attacker can intercept the token and the parsed work orders while they are posted to `process:dispatch-api`. The token has not been rotated since the importer was built, so its disclosure can enable later use against the dispatch API and exposure of the work-order traffic; this draft is conditional on the unknown encryption state.

quotes.text: It presents an API token. That token was issued when the importer was built and nobody has rotated it since.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because the flow crosses a trust boundary with unknown transport encryption, though interception requires access to that path. Impact is high because the flow carries a reusable API token that was not rotated, enabling second-order access to the dispatch API in addition to disclosure of business-critical work orders.

mitigations.detail: Set `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:process:schedule-importer>process:dispatch-api>post-work-orders` to TLS 1.2+ with strict server certificate validation; use mTLS where feasible.

mitigations.summary: Replace and rotate the static API token
mitigations.detail: Move from the long-lived importer token to short-lived, narrowly scoped credentials with automated rotation, then revoke and replace the existing token.

claims.title: Crew details may be readable on the unverified API-to-database connection
claims.description: `flow:process:dispatch-api>store:dispatch-database>read-write-job-orders` carries job orders, crew names, and crew mobile numbers between `process:dispatch-api` and `store:dispatch-database`, but its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown. If the database connection is unencrypted, an attacker able to observe the production-control-plane path can intercept crew PII and dispatch records in transit. The disclosed records can be used to identify and target specific crews and to map current operational work; this draft is conditional on the unverified database-link encryption.

quotes.text: That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low and conditional because the connection remains within the production control plane and an attacker must gain an on-path position, although its transport encryption is unknown. Impact is high because the flow carries crew names and mobile numbers together with operational job orders, producing irreversible PII disclosure at operational scale.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and authenticate the database connection
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation, and preferably mutual authentication, on `flow:process:dispatch-api>store:dispatch-database>read-write-job-orders`.

mitigations.summary: Reduce sensitive fields on routine database exchanges
mitigations.detail: Separate or protect crew contact fields so operational queries and responses do not carry mobile numbers unless the API operation requires them.

claims.title: A storage copy could expose the dispatch database if at-rest encryption is absent
claims.description: `store:dispatch-database` contains job orders, crew names, and crew mobile numbers, but its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If this unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains a database volume, backup, snapshot, or decommissioned media can read the database directly without authenticating through `process:dispatch-api`. The raw copy exposes the crew PII and business-critical dispatch corpus and can support targeted attacks against live operations; this draft is conditional and does not assert that encryption at rest is absent.

quotes.text: How the database is protected at rest is not written down anywhere.
That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:dispatch-database` has unknown at-rest encryption and backup or media access bypasses application authentication, although the control may be present. Impact is high because one raw copy discloses the database's crew PII and business-critical job-order corpus irreversibly.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for database copies
mitigations.detail: Determine the actual `encryption_at_rest` posture of `store:dispatch-database`, then enforce managed-key encryption on the primary database, backups, snapshots, replicas, and decommissioned media.
Separate backup/export permissions from application access, restrict who can use decryption keys, and audit snapshot creation and restore operations.

claims.title: Archived schedule copies may be readable if the file store lacks at-rest encryption
claims.description: `store:schedule-archive` retains every XML document downloaded from the scheduling partner, while its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If the corporate file-store folder is not encrypted at rest, an attacker holding a copied volume, backup, or other storage-layer artifact can read the archived schedule documents without using `process:schedule-importer`. The accumulated archive exposes tomorrow's planned work over time and can reveal operational patterns; this draft is conditional on resolving the at-rest protection.

quotes.text: It writes each document it downloads into the schedule archive, a folder on the corporate file store.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because `store:schedule-archive` has unknown at-rest encryption and storage copies can bypass the normal application path. Impact is medium because the archive holds every downloaded XML schedule document, tagged as business-critical data, enabling disclosure of planned work over time.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt the archive and all retained copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the at-rest posture of `store:schedule-archive` and require managed-key encryption for the file store, its backups, snapshots, and replicas.

mitigations.summary: Apply least privilege to archive access
mitigations.detail: Restrict folder and backup-reader permissions to the importer and explicitly approved operational readers; audit bulk reads and exports.

claims.title: Code running in the dispatch API can read the dispatch database through the API's own access
claims.description: `process:dispatch-api` reads and writes `store:dispatch-database` over `flow:process:dispatch-api>store:dispatch-database>read-write-job-orders`. An attacker who obtains code execution in `process:dispatch-api` can use the API's existing database access to read job orders, crew names, and crew mobile numbers. This is distinct from a storage-copy threat: at-rest encryption does not prevent an authorized application session from receiving decrypted rows. The disclosure can expose the full crew and dispatch corpus and enable targeting of named personnel and live work; the model does not state the database authorization scope, so the breadth of the inherited read access requires confirmation.

quotes.text: The dispatch API reads and writes the dispatch database.
That database holds the job orders, the crew names and the crew mobile numbers.

severity.justification: Likelihood is low because `process:dispatch-api` is internal to the production control plane and the attacker must first run code in that component. Impact is high because the API's stated read path reaches `store:dispatch-database`, which contains crew names, mobile numbers, and job orders.

mitigations.summary: Scope the dispatch API database identity to minimum read access
mitigations.detail: Use a dedicated database principal limited to the rows and columns each API operation needs, separating sensitive crew contact data from routine dispatch operations.

mitigations.summary: Detect anomalous database reads by the API
mitigations.detail: Audit and alert on bulk, atypical, or contact-data-heavy reads made through the database identity used by `process:dispatch-api`.
